entries.originalText: Consider now the lively examples of the holy fathers, in whom shone forth real perfectness and religion, and thou shalt see how little, even as nothing, is all that we do.
entries.modernizedText: Consider now the living examples of the holy fathers, in whom real perfection and religion shone forth, and you will see how little, indeed how nearly nothing, is all that we do.

entries.originalText: Ah!
entries.modernizedText: Ah!

entries.originalText: What is our life when compared to theirs?
entries.modernizedText: What is our life when compared to theirs?

entries.originalText: They, saints and friends of Christ as they were, served the Lord in hunger and thirst, in cold and nakedness, in labour and weariness, in watchings and fastings, in prayer and holy meditations, in persecutions and much rebuke.
entries.modernizedText: They, saints and friends of Christ as they were, served the Lord in hunger and thirst, in cold and nakedness, in labor and weariness, in watchings and fastings, in prayer and holy meditations, in persecutions and much rebuke.

entries.originalText: O how many and grievous tribulations did the Apostles, Martyrs, Confessors, Virgins, endure; and all others who would walk in the footsteps of Christ.
entries.modernizedText: Oh, how many grievous tribulations the Apostles, Martyrs, Confessors, Virgins, and all others who would walk in the footsteps of Christ endured!

entries.originalText: For they hated their souls in this world that they might keep them unto life eternal.
entries.modernizedText: For they hated their souls in this world so that they might keep them for eternal life.

entries.originalText: O how strict and retired a life was that of the holy fathers who dwelt in the desert! what long and grievous temptations they did suffer! how often were they assaulted by the enemy! what frequent and fervid prayers did they offer unto God! what strict fasts did they endure! what fervent zeal and desire after spiritual profit did they manifest! how bravely did they fight that their vices might not gain the mastery! how entirely and steadfastly did they reach after God!
entries.modernizedText: Oh, how strict and secluded was the life of the holy fathers who dwelt in the desert! What long and grievous temptations they suffered! How often they were assaulted by the enemy! What frequent and fervent prayers they offered to God! What strict fasts they endured! What fervent zeal and desire for spiritual benefit they showed! How bravely they fought so that their vices might not gain mastery! How completely and steadfastly they reached toward God!

entries.originalText: By day they laboured, and at night they gave themselves ofttimes unto prayer; yea, even when they were labouring they ceased not from mental prayer.
entries.modernizedText: By day they labored, and at night they often gave themselves to prayer; indeed, even when they were laboring they did not cease from mental prayer.

entries.originalText: They spent their whole time profitably; every hour seemed short for retirement with God; and through the great sweetness of contemplation, even the need of bodily refreshment was forgotten.
entries.modernizedText: They spent their whole time profitably; every hour seemed short for solitude with God, and through the great sweetness of contemplation, even the need for bodily refreshment was forgotten.

entries.originalText: They renounced all riches, dignities, honours, friends, kinsmen; they desired nothing from the world; they ate the bare necessaries of life; they were unwilling to minister to the body even in necessity.
entries.modernizedText: They renounced all riches, dignities, honors, friends, and relatives; they desired nothing from the world; they ate only the bare necessities of life; they were unwilling to attend to the body even in necessity.

entries.originalText: Thus were they poor in earthly things, but rich above measure in grace and virtue.
entries.modernizedText: Thus they were poor in earthly things, but rich beyond measure in grace and virtue.

entries.originalText: Though poor to the outer eye, within they were filled with grace and heavenly benedictions.
entries.modernizedText: Though poor to the outward eye, within they were filled with grace and heavenly blessings.

entries.originalText: They were strangers to the world, but unto God they were as kinsmen and friends.
entries.modernizedText: They were strangers to the world, but to God they were as relatives and friends.

entries.originalText: They seemed unto themselves as of no reputation, and in the world’s eyes contemptible; but in the sight of God they were precious and beloved.
entries.modernizedText: They seemed to themselves to be of no reputation, and contemptible in the world’s eyes; but in the sight of God they were precious and beloved.

entries.originalText: They stood fast in true humility, they lived in simple obedience, they walked in love and patience; and thus they waxed strong in spirit, and obtained great favour before God.
entries.modernizedText: They stood firm in true humility, lived in simple obedience, and walked in love and patience; and thus they grew strong in spirit and obtained great favor before God.

entries.originalText: To all religious men they were given as an example, and they ought more to provoke us unto good livings than the number of the lukewarm tempteth to carelessness of life.
entries.modernizedText: They were given as an example to all religious people, and they ought to stir us to good living more than the number of the lukewarm tempts us to carelessness of life.

entries.originalText: O how great was the love of all religious persons at the beginning of this sacred institution!
entries.modernizedText: Oh, how great was the love of all religious people at the beginning of this sacred institution!

entries.originalText: O what devoutness of prayer! what rivalry in holiness! what strict discipline was observed! what reverence and obedience under the rule of the master showed they in all things!
entries.modernizedText: Oh, what devotion in prayer! What rivalry in holiness! What strict discipline was observed! What reverence and obedience under the rule of the master they showed in all things!

entries.originalText: The traces of them that remain until now testify that they were truly holy and perfect men, who fighting so bravely trod the world underfoot.
entries.modernizedText: The traces of them that remain until now testify that they were truly holy and perfect people who, fighting so bravely, trampled the world underfoot.

entries.originalText: Now a man is counted great if only he be not a transgressor, and if he can only endure with patience what he hath undertaken.
entries.modernizedText: Now a person is counted great if only he is not a transgressor and can endure with patience what he has undertaken.

entries.originalText: O the coldness and negligence of our times, that we so quickly decline from the former love, and it is become a weariness to live, because of sloth and lukewarmness.
entries.modernizedText: Oh, the coldness and negligence of our times, that we so quickly decline from our former love, and living has become wearisome because of sloth and lukewarmness.

entries.originalText: May progress in holiness not wholly fall asleep in thee, who many times hast seen so many examples of devout men!
entries.modernizedText: May progress in holiness not wholly fall asleep in you, who have so many times seen so many examples of devout people!
